```{r read-in}
background <- read.csv("../data/background-clean.csv")
interest <- read.csv("../data/interest-clean.csv")
View(background)
View(interest)
interest$areas
nrow(interest)

sum(background$research == "Yes")
sum(background$research == "No")

bck_x_intrst <- background |>
  left_join(interest, by = "response_id") |>
  mutate(across(ends_with(".prof"), ~ factor(.x, levels = c("beg", "int", "adv")))) |>
  mutate(across(ends_with(".comf"), ~ factor(.x, levels = c("3", "4", "5")))) 

names(which(colSums(is.na(interest)) > 0))
names(which(colSums(is.na(background)) > 0 ))

setdiff(background$response_id, interest$response_id)

bck_x_intrst |> 
  mutate(domains = str_split(domains, ", ")) |>
  unnest(cols = c(domains)) |>
  distinct() |> 
  subset(!duplicated(domains)) |>
  select(domains)

bck_x_intrst[rowSums(is.na(bck_x_intrst)) > 0,]
bck_x_intrst[is.na(bck_x_intrst$type),]
names(which(colSums(is.na(bck_x_intrst)) > 0))
colSums(is.na(bck_x_intrst))
```

To answer our final question, we first want to clean up our data! We are focusing on the variables `type` and `research`. From our data, `type` answers whether the respondent is interested in a research or industry project, and `research` represents whether the respondent has prior supervised research experience. As we can see, Respondent id 1038 and 1046 have NA values under `type`. We excluded these two respondents because their type was unavailable. All of the remainign respondents had complete data on type and research. Among the respondents with a clear answer on prior expereince in supervised research, 23 reported having experience and 24 did not. 



```{r prof and comf summary}
bck_x_intrst |>
  select(ends_with(".prof"), ends_with(".comf")) |>
  mutate(across(ends_with(".prof"), ~ recode(
    .x,
    "adv" = 3,
    "int" = 2,
    "beg" = 1
  ))) |>
  mutate(across(ends_with(".comf"), ~ as.numeric(.x))) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  summarise(
    min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(value, na.rm =TRUE),
    .by = variable
  )


```

From the data, students rated their own proficiency on a three-point scale (beginner = 1, intermediate = 2, advanced = 3). Self-rated proficiency was highest in statistics (mean = 2.65, median = 3), followed by math (mean = 2.41, median = 2) and programming (mean = 2.25, median = 2). No respondent rated themselves a beginner in math or statistics (minimum = 2), while some did in programming (minimum = 1). Overall, students described themselves as intermediate to advanced, with the strongest self-assessment in statistics.


```{r preference in lab or industry compared to 160}

taken160 <- bck_x_intrst |>
  mutate(taken_160 = str_detect(courses, "\\b160\\b"))

names(colSums(is.na(bck_x_intrst)) > 0 )
bck_x_intrst[rowSums(is.na(bck_x_intrst)) > 0, ]

ggplot(taken160, aes(x = type, fill = taken_160)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "count", position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    x = "Industry or Research Lab",
    fill = "Has Taken PSTAT 160?",
    title = "Distribution of Preference for Industry or Lab Split by Taking PSTAT 160"
  )
  
```


```{r proficiency and language}

ggplot(bck_x_intrst, aes(x = prog.prof, fill = language)) +
  geom_bar(stat = 'count', position = 'dodge') +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Prog.prof Against Language Preference",
    x = "programming profficiency",
    fill = "Programming Language"
  )

```

```{r domain proportion against language}

areas_lookup <- tribble(
  ~from, ~to,
  
)

areas <- bck_x_intrst |>
  select(response_id, areas) |>
  mutate(areas = str_replace_all(areas, regex(", generally", ignore_case = TRUE), " (generally)")) |>
  separate_longer_delim(areas, delim = ',')

areas_lang <- bck_x_intrst |>
  select(-areas) |>
  left_join(areas, by = 'response_id') |>
  distinct(response_id, language, areas) |>
  count(areas, language) |>
  left_join(
    bck_x_intrst |>
      distinct(response_id, language) |>
      count(language, name = 'n_lang'),
    by = 'language'
  ) |>
  mutate(prop = n / n_lang) 

areas_lang
bck_x_intrst
nrow(bck_x_intrst)
nrow(areas_lang)

ggplot(areas_lang, aes(x = areas, y = prop, fill = language)) +
  geom_col(position = 'dodge') +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = paste('Areas vs. Language (n=45)'),
    x = "Proportion of Group Interested in Area"
  )
```
